# i18n-keyless-kotlin (Kotlin, Android)

> Keyless i18n for Kotlin and Android. Write the string in your primary language, pass it to `I18nKeyless.t(...)`, and ship 48 languages at runtime with AI translations. No `strings.xml` per language, no resource ids, no translation keys. Add a language without a release.

This file is the whole documentation of the Kotlin library in one Markdown file, meant to be pasted into an LLM context window. Version 3.6.1, protocol v3. The same API key, dashboard and protocol serve the React, React Native, Node, Vue, Angular, Laravel, Rails and Flutter SDKs (see https://docs.i18n-keyless.com/llms.txt).

## Core concepts

- **Keyless**: the source string itself is the translation key. A context (`8 heures` + `durée`) is stored as `8 heures__durée`.
- **Primary language**: the language the source strings are written in. Any of the 48 codes.
- **Supported languages** (48, the App Store localizations), as the `Lang` enum: `ar bn ca zh-Hans zh-Hant hr cs da nl en en-GB fi fr fr-CA de el gu he hi hu id it ja kn ko ms ml mr no or pl pt pt-BR pa ro ru sk sl es es-MX sv ta te th tr uk ur vi`. Enum names are upper case with `_` for the hyphen: `Lang.PT_BR`, `Lang.ZH_HANS`, `Lang.EN_GB`. `lang.code` is the wire string.
- **Storage**: `Storage` (three synchronous methods). `FileStorage(dir)` or a `SharedPreferences` adapter on a device, `MemoryStorage()` by default.
- **Device or server**: `server = false` (default) is a device with a persisted id and usage analytics; `server = true` (Ktor, Spring, a build step) sends no id and no usage.
- **AI translations**: on a cache miss the server generates the translation, stores it, and the next dictionary fetch brings it to the device.
- **Overrides**: edit a translation in the dashboard (https://i18n-keyless.com/dashboard) or use `forceTemporary` from code.
- **Namespaces**: an optional per-call partition (`namespace = "checkout"`) so a device fetches and stores only the slice it renders. Not a semantic key. Reserved default: `default`.
- **User generated content**: pass `originLanguage` for a string written by a user in another language.
- **API key**: https://i18n-keyless.com/#get-api-key. Required in every mode.
- **Zero dependencies**: `HttpURLConnection`, `java.util.concurrent`, a built-in JSON codec. Nothing transitive, nothing to shade on Android.

## Installation

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
implementation("io.github.arnaudambro:i18n-keyless-kotlin:3.6.1")
```

```kotlin
import io.i18nkeyless.*

// Application.onCreate() on Android, main() elsewhere
I18nKeyless.init(I18nKeylessConfig(
    apiKey = "YOUR_API_KEY",
    languages = LanguagesConfig(primary = Lang.FR, supported = listOf(Lang.FR, Lang.EN)),
    storage = FileStorage(context.filesDir.resolve("i18n-keyless")),
))
```

`init` returns a `CompletableFuture` at once: the cache is hydrated on a worker thread, then the bulk fetch and the usage POST run in the background. `initBlocking` waits for the hydration; `I18nKeyless.waitForIdle()` waits for the network (splash screen, tests).

## Usage

```kotlin
// Function path: no trim, no subscription. Notifications, logs, values handed elsewhere.
I18nKeyless.t("Bonjour le monde")
I18nKeyless.t("Bonjour {name}", replace = mapOf("{name}" to user.name))
I18nKeyless.t("8 heures", context = "durée")

// Component path: trims the source text. TextViews and Compose.
textView.text = I18nKeyless.text("Bonjour le monde")

// Language.
I18nKeyless.setLanguage(Lang.EN)   // notifies at once, fetches in the background; returns a future
I18nKeyless.currentLanguage        // Lang.EN
I18nKeyless.supportedLanguages

// Re-render when a translation lands or the language changes (fired on a worker thread).
I18nKeyless.addListener { runOnUiThread { render() } }
```

### Compose

```kotlin
@Composable
fun T(text: String, context: String? = null, replace: Map<String, String>? = null): String {
    val value by produceState(I18nKeyless.text(text, context = context, replace = replace), text, context, replace) {
        val listener = { value = I18nKeyless.text(text, context = context, replace = replace) }
        I18nKeyless.addListener(listener)
        awaitDispose { I18nKeyless.removeListener(listener) }
    }
    return value
}

Text(T("Bonjour {name}", replace = mapOf("{name}" to user.name)))
```

### Per-translation options

Named parameters of `t(...)` and `text(...)`, or a `TranslationOptions` for `translate(...)`:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `context = "durée"` | disambiguates meaning; two contexts are two translations |
| `replace = mapOf("{name}" to user.name)` | interpolation; keys include the delimiters; regex-special characters are literal; an empty replacement keeps the placeholder |
| `namespace = "checkout"` | fetch/storage partition |
| `unpersistedNamespace = true` | memory-only namespace, never persisted, never reported |
| `forceTemporary = mapOf(Lang.EN to "Hi")` | your own translation, sent to the API, arrives with the next fetch |
| `originLanguage = Lang.ES` | the language a user-written string is in |
| `debug = true` | logs the resolution of this string |

### Config (`I18nKeylessConfig`)

| Field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `apiKey` | required |
| `apiUrl` | `https://api.i18n-keyless.com` (self-hosted backend, no trailing slash) |
| `languages` | required: `LanguagesConfig(primary, supported, fallback, initWithDefault, skipCurrentLanguageHydration)` |
| `storage` | `MemoryStorage()` |
| `defaultNamespace` | `default` |
| `server` | `false`; `true` sends `kotlin-server`, no device id, records and sends no usage analytics |
| `handleTranslate`, `getAllTranslations`, `sendTranslationsUsage` | custom handlers replacing the HTTP calls, called on a worker thread |
| `onInit`, `onSetLanguage` | callbacks |
| `debug`, `logger` | `false`, `println` |

The transport is injected on the client: `I18nKeylessClient(api = Api(transport = HttpTransport { request -> HttpResponse(status, statusText, headers, body) }))`.

### Device language at first launch

```kotlin
val tag = Locale.getDefault().toLanguageTag()                                        // "pt-BR"
val lang = resolveLang(tag, supported = listOf(Lang.FR, Lang.EN), fallback = Lang.EN)
// LanguagesConfig(..., initWithDefault = lang)
```

`resolveLang` maps any BCP-47 tag most specific first (`pt-BR`, then `pt`; `zh-TW` is `zh-Hant`; `es-419` is `es-MX`). `Lang.fromCode("pt-BR")` is the exact match. `toAppStoreLocale(Lang.FR)` is `fr-FR`.

## Server (Ktor, Spring, a build step)

`server = true`: `sdk: kotlin-server`, no `unique_id`, no usage analytics, no device id minted; translate-on-miss still works. A client holds one current language, so a server that answers users in several languages keeps one `I18nKeylessClient` per language (each `server = true`, each `setLanguage(lang)` once) and picks the client of the request's language. They share nothing but the API key.

## How it works

1. `t("Bonjour")` looks the key up in the flat cache of the current language, synchronously. Miss: the source text is returned and the key is queued (30 in flight at most, deduplicated by `namespace:key`).
2. The queue posts `POST /translate` per missing key. When it drains, `GET /translate/:lang` fetches the dictionary of every namespace that had a miss, with `If-None-Match` when an ETag is known (a `304` keeps the cache). The answer is merged and persisted per namespace.
3. Transport: 10 s timeout, 3 attempts, 500 ms then 1500 ms backoff on network errors, 429 and 5xx; no retry on other 4xx; never throws; never clears a stored translation. All on daemon worker threads.
4. Identity: a 16-character device id is generated before the first request, persisted under `i18n-keyless-user-id`, and sent as `unique_id` with `sdk: kotlin-client` and `Version: 3.6.1`. It is what the API counts as one user. `clearStorage()` keeps it.
5. Usage analytics: every render records `key__context` with the UTC date under its namespace; the map is POSTed once per `init` and cleared on success. `server = true` disables both.

## Storage adapters

```kotlin
interface Storage {
    fun getItem(key: String): String?
    fun setItem(key: String, value: String)
    fun removeItem(key: String)
}

class SharedPreferencesStorage(private val prefs: SharedPreferences) : Storage {
    override fun getItem(key: String): String? = prefs.getString(key, null)
    override fun setItem(key: String, value: String) = prefs.edit().putString(key, value).apply()
    override fun removeItem(key: String) = prefs.edit().remove(key).apply()
}
```

Keys (identical to the JavaScript SDKs): `i18n-keyless-user-id`, `i18n-keyless-current-language`, `i18n-keyless-translations` (default namespace, JSON), `i18n-keyless-translations__<ns>`, `i18n-keyless-last-refresh`, `i18n-keyless-last-refresh__<ns>`, `i18n-keyless-translations-usage`, `i18n-keyless-namespaces`, `i18n-keyless-origin-namespaces`.

## Testing

```kotlin
val transport = HttpTransport { request ->
    HttpResponse(200, "OK", emptyMap(), """{"ok":true,"data":{"translations":{"Bonjour":"Hello"}},"error":"","message":""}""")
}
val client = I18nKeylessClient(api = Api(transport))
client.initBlocking(I18nKeylessConfig(apiKey = "test", languages = LanguagesConfig(Lang.FR, listOf(Lang.FR, Lang.EN))))
client.setLanguage(Lang.EN).get()
client.waitForIdle()
assertEquals("Hello", client.t("Bonjour"))
```

## Gotchas

- `t()` before `init` returns the source text and does not throw.
- Listeners fire on a worker thread: post to the main thread before touching a view.
- Source strings must be written in the primary language.
- No leading or trailing whitespace inside `t(...)`; `text()` trims.
- A dashboard edit reaches cached devices at the next refresh, not instantly.
- After a language switch, a string with no entry in the new language shows the previous language's text until its translation arrives.
- Two contexts of the same string in one batch make one `POST /translate`; the second is translated on a later render.
- A source string is capped at 2000 characters (`context` and `namespace` at 200). Long-form content is allowed, but a blog post is one translation **per Markdown block** of about 1000 characters: keep the Markdown inside each block, give every block of the document the same `context` (one very short summary of it) and one `namespace` per document. https://docs.i18n-keyless.com/docs/guides/long-form-content
